headline.caveat: Current order value undisclosed. Supermicro built roughly half of the original Colossus racks and supplies GB300 NVL72 racks for Colossus 2 — after xAI had shifted ~$6B of orders to Dell during Supermicro's 2024-25 accounting/DOJ turmoil, later restoring SMCI as a second-source supplier.

realized_to_date.caveat: Colossus 1 deliveries (H100/H200, GB200 era) plus ongoing GB300 racks; neither party discloses totals.

nature_md: Supermicro is one of two rack suppliers (with Dell) for xAI's Colossus supercomputers, having built liquid-cooled racks for the original 100K-GPU cluster and now supplying NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 racks for Colossus 2. The relationship survived a near-death moment: xAI reportedly shifted ~$6B of orders to rivals when Supermicro faced auditor resignation and a DOJ probe (late 2024), then resumed orders as SMCI stabilized — xAI deliberately dual-sources its rack supply. Direct-to-chip liquid cooling co-engineering is the differentiator SMCI retained.

accounting.payer_treatment_md: xAI capitalizes rack purchases as compute infrastructure (or via GPU-leasing SPV structures), depreciated over 4-6 years; split-sourcing between Dell and SMCI is a supply-risk hedge, not a financial structure.
accounting.payee_treatment_md: Supermicro books hardware revenue on delivery; xAI is among its largest single accounts (FY25 revenue ~$22B, 70%+ AI — figures partly UNVERIFIED given its restatement history), making order-shift headlines highly market-moving for SMCI.

both_sides_md: **Bull:** SMCI's liquid-cooling lead and build speed won xAI back despite governance scars — capability trumped credit concerns. **Bear:** the ~$6B order shift showed how fast this revenue evaporates on counterparty doubt, in both directions; concentration cuts against SMCI whenever xAI's capital raising stumbles.
